heroHeadline: Science Journal Confirms: Global Mangroves Have Reversed 40-Year Decline — Net Gain Since 2010
heroSubtitle: A landmark Tulane University study in Science (June 4) using 40 years of NASA Landsat data found that global mangrove forests have reversed their long-term decline — net gains since 2010 have reduced the four-decade loss to roughly 1%, driven by natural regeneration, conservation policy, and climate-driven expansion. Nigeria relocated its Great Green Wall national agency headquarters to Kano (June 4), moving it closer to the Sahel frontline as part of President Tinubu's Renewed Hope Agenda. World Environment Day 2026 was observed globally on June 5, hosted by Azerbaijan under the theme 'Inspired by Nature. For Climate. For Our Future' (#NowForClimate). On June 3, Carbon Brief flagged twin Amazon infrastructure threats: a $75M highway and a 965km railway advanced through Brazil's Supreme Court — even as Amazon deforestation reaches its lowest rate since 2019.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNEP, FAO, UNCCD, IUCN, WRI Global Forest Watch, INPE, CBD, NASA, and Tier 2 science outlets. Pledge figures reflect commitments; verified restoration is substantially lower.
